alerts.title: DTG-associated weight gain and pre-diabetes risk
alerts.message: Guidelines identify rapid weight gain as a risk factor for diabetes in PLHIV on ART. Patient gained 17kg (65→82kg) and BMI rose from 25.6 to 32.4 (obese class I) within 18 months of switching to DTG-based TLD. She now has pre-diabetic fasting glucose (118 mg/dL) and HbA1c (6.1%), plus acanthosis nigricans. DTG is strongly temporally linked: weight gain began after TLD initiation. Evidence against drug attribution: family history of Type 2 Diabetes is an independent contributor. Non-drug causes (dietary, behavioural) should also be considered. No clinician assessment or plan was documented today.

evidence.recommended_action: Assess for DM using the guideline screening tool, counsel on lifestyle modification, and consider DTG-related metabolic effects. Document a formal management plan.

alerts.title: DTG hyperglycaemia screening criteria met
alerts.message: Guidelines require glucose screening for patients transitioning to DTG who have 2 or more risk factors for hyperglycaemia: age ≥30, family history of DM, BMI ≥25 kg/m². This patient has all three risk factors (age 36, mother with Type 2 Diabetes, BMI 32.4). Fasting glucose (118 mg/dL) and HbA1c (6.1%) confirm impaired fasting glucose and pre-diabetes. No clinician plan was documented for diabetes screening, monitoring, or management despite these results.

evidence.recommended_action: Follow the guideline algorithm for screening and management of diabetes. Repeat fasting glucose, initiate lifestyle counselling, and schedule follow-up glucose monitoring.

alerts.title: Dyslipidemia and hypertension compounding metabolic risk
alerts.message: Guidelines note dyslipidemia as a risk factor for diabetes in PLHIV. Patient has an adverse lipid profile: total cholesterol 228 mg/dL, LDL 148 mg/dL, HDL 38 mg/dL, triglycerides 212 mg/dL. BP increased from 118/74 to 138/88 mmHg since TLD initiation, approaching hypertensive range. Obesity (BMI 32.4), pre-diabetes, dyslipidemia, and elevated BP together substantially increase cardiovascular risk. No clinician plan addresses these metabolic abnormalities.

evidence.recommended_action: Evaluate cardiovascular risk, address dyslipidemia and elevated BP with lifestyle modification and pharmacotherapy if indicated, and document a management plan.

alerts.title: No clinician assessment or plan documented
alerts.message: No clinician assessment or plan was documented for this visit despite significant findings: 17kg weight gain, new-onset pre-diabetes, dyslipidemia, elevated BP, and acanthosis nigricans. Guidelines describe a structured algorithm for DM screening and management among patients on ART. The absence of any documented plan represents a guideline deviation and leaves multiple metabolic abnormalities unaddressed.

evidence.recommended_action: Document a comprehensive assessment and management plan addressing weight gain, pre-diabetes, dyslipidemia, and elevated BP per guideline recommendations.
